newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: COMESA blames "enemies" for members' defections.
newsitem.headline: COMESA blames "enemies" for members' defections.

text.p: The secretary-general of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) on Tuesday blamed "enemies of Africa" for a growing split between two African trade groupings.
Mozambique and Lesotho recently gave notice that they would withdraw from COMESA in favour of the 12-member Southern African Development Community (SADC) dominated by South Africa.
COMESA secretary-general Bingu Wa Muthraika told a Lusaka news conference that the move by Mozambique and Lesotho had been engineered by "forces" which he did not name.
"We believe the enemies of Africa are trying to destroy us (COMESA) because we have been so successful. We are the most successful economic grouping in eastern and southern Africa," Muthraika said.
He said the same enemies, whom he declined to name, were behind the collapse of the East African Community of Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania several years ago.
"They picked out the weaklings in the grouping and used them to create a split. That is what they are now doing to COMESA," he said.
He urged Mozambique and Lesotho to reconsider, saying both had more to gain from membership of COMESA, which had more members than SADC.

"COMESA is useful to both Mozambique and Lesotho as it was designed to be a vehicle to enable the countries launch an export drive not only in the common market but also to the rest of the world," he added.
Mozambique and Lesotho said they preferred to work alongside SADC. They said COMESA and SADC duplicated efforts, and COMESA was too large to address their specific concerns.

COMESA states are Angola, Burundi, Comoros, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Rwanda, Sudan, Swaziland, Tanzania, Uganda, Zaire, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
SADC comprises Mauritius, Angola, Lesotho, Swaziland, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Mozambique, Tanzania, Malawi, South Africa and Botswana.
